## What this document does

`growth.cpp`'s needle-growth demand (the real, carbon/nitrogen-costed
signal `sugar_model.cpp` uses, not a parallel pathway) is

$$\text{needles}_t = m_N \cdot GN_t \cdot \frac{HH_{\text{yr}-1}}{h_{\text{inc}}}$$

`GN_t` is today's within-season phenology shape; `last_year_HH` is a
one-year-lagged *vigor proxy* - the idea (Schiestl-Aalto et al. 2015 eqn 4's
lagged sink-demand structure) is that needle primordia are preformed in last
year's bud, so this year's needle growth potential should scale with how
vigorously the tree grew last year, not this year's conditions directly.
`h_increment` is a fixed site constant (309, Väriö 2010-2015 mean annual
height increment) that turns `last_year_HH` into a relative-to-average
ratio.

Since 2026-11-05, `height_diameter_correction` (Mäkelä 1999's
structural-balance control) also damps `HH` directly when simulated height
has drifted ahead of diameter. That means a low `last_year_HH` can now mean
either of two different things - a genuinely weak growth year, or the
correction doing its job - and the needle-growth equation above can't tell
them apart. This notebook checks how much that actually matters in
practice, and whether last year's **ring width / diameter growth** would be
a cleaner lagged vigor signal instead, since diameter is explicitly the
correction's *uncorrected* reference (`H_bal = alpha_H * D_current`,
`growth.cpp`) - never itself damped by it.

```{r libraries}
devtools::load_all(quiet = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)

pub_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position  = "bottom")
```

## 1  Setup

Same `h0`/`D0`/weather as `height_correction.Rmd`, so this run starts at
the same point (12m height, 1998-2022) as the notebook that originally
validated `height_diameter_correction`.

```{r setup-data}
data_directory  <- "~/Documents/CASSIA_Calibration/Processed_Data/"
loaded_data     <- load_data(data_directory)

new_parameters  <- rep(0.5, 27)
parameters_2015 <- initialize_parameters(calibration = FALSE, new_parameters)

parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("h0"),          "Hyde"] <- 12
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("D0"),          "Hyde"] <- 0.1646
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("GPP_mean"),    "Hyde"] <- 463.8833
parameters_2015$parameters_test[c("GPP_initial"), "Hyde"] <- 460.0
```

```{r setup-weather}
weather_preles <- data.table::fread("~/Documents/CASSIA/data/ERA5_CASSIA_preles.csv")

weather_1998_2022 <- weather_preles[
  weather_preles$date >= as.Date("1998-01-01") &
  weather_preles$date <= as.Date("2022-12-31"), ]
weather_1998_2022$dates <- as.Date(weather_1998_2022$date)
dates_1998_2022 <- weather_1998_2022$dates
```

Two runs, identical except for `height_diameter_correction` - isolates
exactly what the correction changes about the height/vigor signal, with
nothing else varying.

```{r run-model, cache=TRUE}
run_nitrogen <- function(height_diameter_correction) {
  CASSIA_cpp(
    weather                    = weather_1998_2022,
    site                       = "Hyde",
    pPREL                      = c(parameters_2015$pPREL, parameters_2015$N_parameters),
    parameters                 = parameters_2015$parameters_test,
    common                     = common_p,
    ratios                     = ratios_p,
    sperling                   = parameters_2015$sperling_test,
    needle_mass_in             = 0,
    Throughfall                = parameters_2015$Throughfall,
    photosynthesis_as_input    = FALSE,
    nitrogen_balance           = 25,
    nitrogen_change            = FALSE,
    nitrogen_contrast          = FALSE,
    preles                     = TRUE,
    fAPAR_Tian                 = TRUE,
    organ_level_sugar          = FALSE,
    needle_mass_grows          = TRUE,
    height_diameter_correction = height_diameter_correction
  )
}

CASSIA_uncorrected <- run_nitrogen(FALSE)
CASSIA_corrected    <- run_nitrogen(TRUE)
```

## 2  Annual height growth vs. annual ring width growth

Neither `last_year_HH` (an internal C++ state) nor the daily `height_growth`
output is a 1:1 reproduction of `HH` itself (`height_growth` already has
`B0`/`CH`/`form_factor` folded in) - but the question that matters here is
simpler than reproducing `HH` exactly: **does the correction's damping show
up as a dip in the annual height signal that ring width doesn't share?**
That's answerable directly from existing output columns, by comparing each
year's total `height_growth` against that year's total `ring_width`,
indexed to their own first year so the very different units don't matter.

```{r annual-totals, cache=TRUE}
annual_totals <- function(run, label) {
  df <- data.frame(year = run$Growth$year,
                    height_growth = run$Growth$height_growth,
                    ring_width    = run$Growth$ring_width)
  agg <- aggregate(cbind(height_growth, ring_width) ~ year, data = df, FUN = sum)
  agg$height_index <- agg$height_growth / agg$height_growth[1]
  agg$ring_index    <- agg$ring_width / agg$ring_width[1]
  agg$run <- label
  agg
}

totals_uncorrected <- annual_totals(CASSIA_uncorrected, "Uncorrected")
totals_corrected    <- annual_totals(CASSIA_corrected, "Corrected (height_diameter_correction)")
totals_all <- rbind(totals_uncorrected, totals_corrected)
```

```{r vigor-signal-plot, fig.height=7}
signal_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(year = totals_all$year, value = totals_all$height_index,
             signal = "Annual height growth (index)", run = totals_all$run),
  data.frame(year = totals_all$year, value = totals_all$ring_index,
             signal = "Annual ring width growth (index)", run = totals_all$run)
)

ggplot(signal_long, aes(x = year, y = value, colour = signal)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ run, ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c(
    "Annual height growth (index)"     = "#1b7837",
    "Annual ring width growth (index)" = "#762a83"
  )) +
  labs(title = "Candidate lagged vigor signals, indexed to their own 1998 value",
       subtitle = "If the two signals move together, the correction isn't distorting the vigor proxy much; if they diverge, last_year_HH and a ring-width equivalent would disagree about how 'vigorous' a year was",
       x = NULL, y = "Index (1998 = 1)") +
  pub_theme
```

```{r vigor-signal-correlation}
cor_uncorrected <- cor(totals_uncorrected$height_index, totals_uncorrected$ring_index)
cor_corrected    <- cor(totals_corrected$height_index, totals_corrected$ring_index)
cat("Correlation between the two annual signals:\n")
cat("  Uncorrected run: ", round(cor_uncorrected, 3), "\n")
cat("  Corrected run:   ", round(cor_corrected, 3), "\n")
```

## 3  Comparison against the original R reference model

Three copies of the pre-C++-port R implementation exist
(`~/Downloads/model.R`, `~/Downloads/CASSIA-Varrio_J(3)/model.R`,
`~/Documents/Original Model/model.R`) - all three use the identical
needle-growth line:

```r
GH <- g.sH * fH * LH * soil_moisture_effect_s_growth
HH <- HH0 + cumsum(GH)
...
needle.pot.growth <- m.N * GN * (max(HH) / h_increment)
```

This is **not actually a one-year lag**. `HH0` is a fixed scalar constant
(`parameters_Varrio.R`: `HH0 <- 10`), never updated between years, and
`GH`/`HH` are computed as full-year vectors in one vectorized pass before
the needle line runs - so `max(HH)` is simply *that same year's own final
cumulative height growth*, known because the R model processes a whole
year of weather at once rather than day-by-day. Every day of a given
year's `needle.pot.growth` uses the identical value: the total height
growth that year eventually reaches.

That's not something the C++ port could keep unchanged - `CASSIA.cpp`
runs online, one day at a time, so October's height growth genuinely
isn't known yet when April's needle growth is being computed. Lagging to
*last* year's total (`last_year_HH`) is the closest causal substitute
available in a day-by-day loop, not an arbitrary design choice -
Sect. 0's "lagged sink-demand" framing (Schiestl-Aalto et al. 2015 eqn 4)
describes the biological motivation for using *some* vigor proxy at all,
not necessarily a one-year lag specifically; the R model's own version
of that same idea uses the current year, which simulation architecture
alone rules out for the C++ port.

Two things worth noting for Sect. 0's proposed fix in that light:

- The R model never references diameter/ring width for needle growth at
  all (`grep` for pipe/Makela/ring-width terms against `model.R` returns
  nothing) - so there's no R-model precedent either for or against the
  ring-width swap. It would be a genuinely new design decision, not a
  reversion to something the R model already did.
- `h_increment` itself is inherited from the R model almost unchanged:
  `parameters_Varrio.R`'s `h_increment <- 120.00` (Väriö) vs. the C++
  repo's Hyde value of 309.0938 - same comment wording ("mean height
  increment"), different site calibration. There is no R-model
  equivalent constant for ring width to inherit the way `h_increment`
  was - a `d_increment`-style constant would need its own calibration
  from scratch, not a port of an existing R value.

### 3.1  Running it: `tests_c++_against_R.Rmd`'s own validation harness, height vs. diameter proxy

Rather than a fresh R reimplementation, this reuses
`tests_c++_against_R.Rmd`'s existing, already-validated comparison: the
package's stored real R-model reference output (`Hyde_daily_original`,
Hyde 2015-2017) against `weather_original` (the same weather SPP itself
runs on, not ERA5), with `tests = TRUE` - as that notebook already does.
That notebook's own Sect. 2 attributes the model's one known small
systematic mismatch - height and needle growth matching at r &asymp; 0.98
instead of the  &ge;0.99 everything else manages - to exactly this lag
(`max(HH)` vs `last_year_HH`).

**`tests = TRUE` is not a neutral setting for this specific comparison,
though, and the plots below are read with that in mind.** It hardcodes
`LH` *and* `LN` to fixed per-year constants for 2016-2018
(`growth.cpp`, two separate `if (boolsettings.tests)` blocks) chosen
specifically so the C++ height/needle trajectories reproduce the R
reference closely - but it does **not** touch `LD` (diameter's own rate
parameter), which still runs through its normal `LD_estim` estimation
either way. So `last_year_HH` (the `TRUE` setting) is built from a height
trajectory that was deliberately hand-calibrated to match R, while
`last_year_ring_width` (the `FALSE` setting) is built from a diameter
trajectory that was given no such treatment - not a fair, symmetric test
of "which signal is intrinsically the better vigor proxy," and a real risk
that it mechanically favours `TRUE` regardless of which one is actually
better. Sect. 3.1.7 checks this directly by rerunning with `tests = FALSE`
(both `LH` and `LD` on equal footing, the model's normal operating mode) -
the headline finding survives, but by a smaller margin than the
`tests = TRUE` numbers below suggest on their own.

```{r cpp-vs-r-setup, cache=TRUE}
data("weather_original")
data("Hyde_daily_original")

weather_original$dates <- as.Date(
  strptime(paste(rep(2015:2017, times = c(365, 366, 365)), weather_original$X),
           format = "%Y %j"))

run_tests <- function(growth_proxy_height) {
  CASSIA_cpp(weather = weather_original, site = "Hyde", tests = TRUE,
             growth_proxy_height = growth_proxy_height)
}

out_height <- run_tests(TRUE)
out_diam   <- run_tests(FALSE)

orig <- Hyde_daily_original[Hyde_daily_original$year %in% 2015:2017, ]
orig$dates <- as.Date(strptime(paste(orig$year, orig$day), format = "%Y %j"))

new_g_height <- out_height$Growth; new_g_height$dates <- weather_original$dates
new_g_diam   <- out_diam$Growth;   new_g_diam$dates   <- weather_original$dates
new_su_height <- out_height$Sugar; new_su_height$dates <- weather_original$dates
new_su_diam   <- out_diam$Sugar;   new_su_diam$dates   <- weather_original$dates

no_trees <- 1010
three_colours <- c("Original R" = "black", "C++ height proxy" = "firebrick", "C++ diam proxy" = "#1b7837")

make_triple <- function(df_height, df_diam, orig_col, cpp_col, title, y_lab = "kg C stem⁻¹ day⁻¹") {
  df <- data.frame(
    dates = rep(orig$dates, 3),
    value = c(orig[[orig_col]],
              df_height[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, df_height$dates)],
              df_diam[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, df_diam$dates)]),
    Model = factor(rep(names(three_colours), each = nrow(orig)), levels = names(three_colours))
  )
  ggplot(df, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = Model)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = three_colours) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = y_lab, colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

#### 3.1.1  Summary metrics

```{r cpp-vs-r-metrics}
make_metric_row <- function(cpp_col, orig_col, label) {
  om <- mean(orig[[orig_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  nh <- mean(new_g_height[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, new_g_height$dates)], na.rm = TRUE)
  nd <- mean(new_g_diam[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, new_g_diam$dates)], na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(Variable = label,
             `Orig mean` = round(om, 6),
             `C++ height mean` = round(nh, 6), `Ratio height` = round(nh / om, 4),
             `C++ diam mean`   = round(nd, 6), `Ratio diam`    = round(nd / om, 4),
             check.names = FALSE)
}

metrics3 <- rbind(
  make_metric_row("bud_growth",    "bud",          "Bud growth (actual)"),
  make_metric_row("diameter_growth","wall_daily",  "Diameter growth (actual)"),
  make_metric_row("needle_growth", "needle_daily", "Needle growth (actual)"),
  make_metric_row("root_growth",   "root_daily",   "Root growth (actual)"),
  make_metric_row("height_growth", "height_daily", "Height growth (actual)"),
  make_metric_row("bud_growth_potential",    "bud",          "Bud growth (potential)"),
  make_metric_row("wall_growth_potential",   "wall_daily",   "Diameter growth (potential)"),
  make_metric_row("needle_growth_potential", "needle_daily", "Needle growth (potential)"),
  make_metric_row("roots_growth_potential",  "root_daily",   "Root growth (potential)"),
  make_metric_row("height_growth_potential", "height_daily", "Height growth (potential)"),
  make_metric_row("respiration_growth",      "Rg", "Respiration (growth)"),
  make_metric_row("respiration_maintenance", "Rm", "Respiration (maintenance)")
)

kable(metrics3, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "Mean values over 2015-2017; ratio = C++ / original R")
```

#### 3.1.2  Growth variables: time series

```{r cpp-vs-r-growth-plots, fig.height = 16}
g1 <- make_triple(new_g_height, new_g_diam, "bud",          "bud_growth",     "Bud growth")
g2 <- make_triple(new_g_height, new_g_diam, "wall_daily",   "diameter_growth","Diameter (wall) growth")
g3 <- make_triple(new_g_height, new_g_diam, "needle_daily", "needle_growth",  "Needle growth")
g4 <- make_triple(new_g_height, new_g_diam, "root_daily",   "root_growth",    "Root growth")
g5 <- make_triple(new_g_height, new_g_diam, "height_daily", "height_growth",  "Height growth", y_lab = "m day⁻¹")

(g1 / g2 / g3 / g4 / g5) + plot_layout(ncol = 1, guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Bud, diameter, root and height growth are structurally unaffected by
`growth_proxy_height` (it only enters the needle line) - any visible
difference between the two C++ lines in those four panels is purely
indirect, via the carbon economy (Sect. 3.1.3-3.1.4). Needle growth is
where the direct effect shows.

#### 3.1.3  Carbon storage

```{r cpp-vs-r-storage-plots, fig.height = 8}
s1 <- make_triple(new_su_height, new_su_diam, "sugar",        "sugar",       "Sugar pool",    "kg C stem⁻¹")
s2 <- make_triple(new_su_height, new_su_diam, "starch",       "starch",      "Starch pool",   "kg C stem⁻¹")
s3 <- make_triple(new_su_height, new_su_diam, "storage_term", "storage",     "Storage term (carbon availability fraction, 0-1)", "fraction")

(s1 / s2 / s3) + plot_layout(ncol = 1, guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

#### 3.1.4  GPP

`growth_proxy_height` has no path into photosynthesis - GPP is computed
upstream of growth entirely, so the two C++ lines below should be
(and are) identical; shown for completeness/as a sanity check, not
because a difference was expected.

```{r cpp-vs-r-gpp-plot}
gpp_df <- data.frame(
  dates = rep(orig$dates, 3),
  value = c(orig$P,
            (out_height$Preles$GPP / no_trees * 10)[match(orig$dates, weather_original$dates)],
            (out_diam$Preles$GPP / no_trees * 10)[match(orig$dates, weather_original$dates)]),
  Model = factor(rep(names(three_colours), each = nrow(orig)), levels = names(three_colours))
)

ggplot(gpp_df, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = Model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = three_colours) +
  labs(title = "GPP per stem", x = NULL, y = "kg C stem⁻¹ day⁻¹", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom")
```

#### 3.1.5  Potential vs. actual growth, both settings

The R model only ever computed potential growth (no carbon-storage gate) -
this panel is C++-internal only, comparing each setting's own potential
vs. actual needle growth (bud shown too, as the unaffected reference).

```{r cpp-vs-r-pot-act-plots, fig.height = 9}
pot_act_cols <- c("Potential" = "grey50", "Actual" = "firebrick")

make_pot_act_run <- function(df, title) {
  d <- data.frame(
    dates = rep(df$dates, 2),
    value = c(df$needle_growth_potential, df$needle_growth),
    Type  = rep(c("Potential", "Actual"), each = nrow(df))
  )
  ggplot(d, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = Type)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pot_act_cols) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = "kg C stem⁻¹ day⁻¹", colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom")
}

pa1 <- make_pot_act_run(new_g_height, "Needle growth, potential vs. actual - height proxy")
pa2 <- make_pot_act_run(new_g_diam,   "Needle growth, potential vs. actual - diam proxy")

(pa1 / pa2) + plot_layout(ncol = 1, guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

#### 3.1.6  Respiration

```{r cpp-vs-r-respiration-plots, fig.height = 8}
r1 <- make_triple(new_g_height, new_g_diam, "Rg", "respiration_growth",      "Growth respiration")
r2 <- make_triple(new_g_height, new_g_diam, "Rm", "respiration_maintenance", "Maintenance respiration")
```

### 3.1.7  What this actually shows (under `tests = TRUE`)

The height proxy is the closer match to the real R model here: needle
growth (actual and potential, identical in this comparison) comes out at
1.0100&times; the R reference with `growth_proxy_height = TRUE`, vs.
1.0451&times; with `FALSE` - the height-proxy error is less than a
quarter the size of the diameter-proxy's. The starch-pool plot
(Sect. 3.1.3) shows this visibly, not just in the table: `TRUE` (red)
sits almost exactly on the R reference (black) while `FALSE` (green)
runs visibly lower every year. Needle growth itself (Sect. 3.1.2) looks
nearly identical between the two settings at this resolution - the gap is
there (the table) but small enough over three years to not read clearly
by eye.

But per the caveat above, `tests = TRUE` hand-calibrates `LH` (feeding
`TRUE`'s signal) while leaving `LD` (feeding `FALSE`'s) on its normal
estimation - so this 1.0% vs. 4.5% gap could just be measuring whose
input got the special treatment, not which signal is intrinsically
better. Sect. 3.1.8 checks that directly.

### 3.1.8  Checking the confound: `tests = FALSE`

Same two runs, `tests = FALSE` this time - `LH` and `LD` are both on
their normal estimation (`LH_estim`/`LD_estim`, the model's usual
operating mode, same as every other run in this notebook). Neither
setting gets hand-calibrated help now.

```{r cpp-vs-r-tests-false, cache=TRUE}
out_height_nt <- CASSIA_cpp(weather = weather_original, site = "Hyde", tests = FALSE, growth_proxy_height = TRUE)
out_diam_nt   <- CASSIA_cpp(weather = weather_original, site = "Hyde", tests = FALSE, growth_proxy_height = FALSE)
g_h_nt <- out_height_nt$Growth; g_h_nt$dates <- weather_original$dates
g_d_nt <- out_diam_nt$Growth;   g_d_nt$dates <- weather_original$dates
su_h_nt <- out_height_nt$Sugar; su_h_nt$dates <- weather_original$dates
su_d_nt <- out_diam_nt$Sugar;   su_d_nt$dates <- weather_original$dates

check_cols <- c(needle_growth = "needle_daily", height_growth = "height_daily",
                diameter_growth = "wall_daily", bud_growth = "bud", root_growth = "root_daily")
confound_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(check_cols), function(col) {
  origcol <- check_cols[[col]]
  nh <- mean(g_h_nt[[col]][match(orig$dates, g_h_nt$dates)], na.rm = TRUE)
  nd <- mean(g_d_nt[[col]][match(orig$dates, g_d_nt$dates)], na.rm = TRUE)
  om <- mean(orig[[origcol]], na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(Variable = col, `Ratio height` = round(nh / om, 4), `Ratio diam` = round(nd / om, 4),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))

kable(confound_check, align = c("l", "r", "r"),
      caption = "tests = FALSE: both LH and LD on normal estimation, no hand-calibration either side")
```

The ordering survives: height proxy still beats diameter proxy for needle
growth (4.6% vs. 7.2% off the R reference), and `height_growth` itself is
now visibly off too (2.7%, vs. an exact match under `tests = TRUE`) since
it's no longer hand-calibrated either - confirming that difference really
was `tests = TRUE`'s doing, not a property of the underlying model.
`diameter_growth`'s own ratio (1.0033) is identical under both `tests`
settings, as expected (`LD` was never touched by `tests` in the first
place). So the confound inflated the gap (1.0 vs. 4.5 under `tests = TRUE`
narrows to 4.6 vs. 7.2 under `tests = FALSE`) but didn't fabricate the
direction of it - height genuinely tracks the real R model's needle
growth better than diameter does, over this three-year window, with or
without the hand-calibration.

That's still not a contradiction of Sect. 2/3's finding: this 2015-2017
window is far too short for `height_diameter_correction`'s multi-decade
drift to have compounded into anything visible yet (Sect. 2 needed the
better part of two decades to show the height-based signal's monotonic
decline). At this horizon, switching to `growth_proxy_height = FALSE`
would trade a long-run artifact (real, but only visible over decades) for
a smaller but real degradation in the model's short-run match to its own
validation reference. Which trade-off is worth making depends on the run
length anything downstream actually cares about.

### 3.1.9  All three side by side: hand-calibrated height, normal height, normal diameter

The three C++ variants that actually matter, on one plot each, against
the real R reference: `tests = TRUE` + height proxy (the hand-calibrated
best case from Sect. 3.1.1-3.1.6), `tests = FALSE` + height proxy, and
`tests = FALSE` + diameter proxy (both normal-operation, Sect. 3.1.8).
`tests = TRUE` + diameter proxy is left out deliberately - with `LH`
calibrated for the height pathway but paired with the diameter-based
reference instead, it doesn't correspond to any real operating mode.

```{r cpp-vs-r-quad-setup}
quad_colours <- c("Original R" = "black",
                   "C++ tests=TRUE, height"  = "firebrick",
                   "C++ tests=FALSE, height" = "#e08214",
                   "C++ tests=FALSE, diam"   = "#1b7837")

make_quad <- function(df_a, df_b, df_c, orig_col, cpp_col, title, y_lab = "kg C stem⁻¹ day⁻¹") {
  df <- data.frame(
    dates = rep(orig$dates, 4),
    value = c(orig[[orig_col]],
              df_a[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, df_a$dates)],
              df_b[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, df_b$dates)],
              df_c[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, df_c$dates)]),
    Model = factor(rep(names(quad_colours), each = nrow(orig)), levels = names(quad_colours))
  )
  ggplot(df, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = Model)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = quad_colours) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = y_lab, colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r cpp-vs-r-quad-needle, fig.height = 5}
make_quad(new_g_height, g_h_nt, g_d_nt, "needle_daily", "needle_growth", "Needle growth, all three C++ variants")
```

```{r cpp-vs-r-quad-starch, fig.height = 5}
make_quad(new_su_height, su_h_nt, su_d_nt, "starch", "starch", "Starch pool, all three C++ variants", "kg C stem⁻¹")
```

```{r cpp-vs-r-quad-metrics}
make_quad_row <- function(orig_col, cpp_col, label) {
  om <- mean(orig[[orig_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  a  <- mean(new_g_height[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, new_g_height$dates)], na.rm = TRUE)
  b  <- mean(g_h_nt[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, g_h_nt$dates)], na.rm = TRUE)
  cc <- mean(g_d_nt[[cpp_col]][match(orig$dates, g_d_nt$dates)], na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(Variable = label,
             `tests=TRUE, height` = round(a / om, 4),
             `tests=FALSE, height` = round(b / om, 4),
             `tests=FALSE, diam` = round(cc / om, 4),
             check.names = FALSE)
}

quad_metrics <- rbind(
  make_quad_row("needle_daily", "needle_growth", "Needle growth"),
  make_quad_row("height_daily", "height_growth", "Height growth"),
  make_quad_row("wall_daily",   "diameter_growth","Diameter growth")
)
kable(quad_metrics, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "Ratio to the real R reference, all three variants")
```

Reading the three against each other rather than just against R: going
from `tests = TRUE` to `tests = FALSE` (both height proxy) is the size of
the hand-calibration's own contribution; going from `tests = FALSE`
height to `tests = FALSE` diameter (both normal operation) is the actual,
uncontaminated height-vs-diameter difference this notebook is asking
about. The starch-pool plot makes both steps visible in 2016-2017: hand-
calibrated height (red) sits closest to R, normal-operation height
(orange) drifts a bit further, and normal-operation diameter (green)
drifts furthest of the three. 2015 is a cleaner read than it first looks,
not a counterexample - `growth.cpp`'s `tests` hardcoding only has values
for 2016-2018 (`if (year == 2016) ... else if (year == 2017) ...`), so
`tests = TRUE` and `tests = FALSE` are *identical* for 2015 regardless of
proxy (verified: `height_growth` matches exactly that year, diverges from
2016 on) - the small 2015 gap visible in the plot is genuinely just
height-vs-diameter, with no hand-calibration in play on either red or
orange yet.

---

## 4  Comparison against the pipe-model mechanism

CASSIA already has two live Mäkelä-style corrections -
`height_diameter_correction` (height vs. diameter) and
`root_leaf_correction` (roots vs. leaf mass, Mäkelä & Valentine 2020's
pipe model, `W_r = alpha_r * W_f`). Both share one structure:

```cpp
// height_diameter_correction (growth.cpp)
H_bal = alpha_H * D_current;                                    // independent target, from a DIFFERENT pool
LH = LH * makela_control_factor(H_bal, H_current, parameters.tau_H);  // damp an existing rate toward it, capped at 1

// root_leaf_correction (growth.cpp)
R_bal = alpha_r * leaf_mass_max_last_year;                       // independent target, from a DIFFERENT pool
GR = GR * state.C_R_year;                                        // damp an existing rate toward it, capped at 1
```

Both are **damping corrections**: an organ's own growth-rate term gets
multiplied by a capped ratio of "where it should be" vs. "where it
is" - two pools cross-checked against each other via an allometric
constant (`alpha_H`, `alpha_r`), never swapping which pool drives a
*different* organ's growth demand.

Plainly: `height_diameter_correction` is making simulated height smaller
every year it's active (Sect. 2-3), and needle growth is still referencing
that shrinking height as its vigor signal - so the needle-growth formula
should reference diameter instead, which the correction never touches.
Fixing this changes the standing needle mass pool, not just the daily
growth flux (`leaf_mass_correction` is what turns `state.needles` into a
real accumulating pool, `leaf_mass`, rather than a memoryless annual-reset
value) - the plot below is the same style as Sect. 2, now tracking
`leaf_mass` (kg C/tree) instead of `needle_growth` (kg C/day).

For completeness: this swap isn't technically a third pipe-model
correction like the other two. `height_diameter_correction`/
`root_leaf_correction` both damp an organ's own growth rate toward an
independent target from a *different* pool, capped at 1
(`makela_control_factor`). `last_year_HH` isn't a target needle growth is
checked against - it's multiplied directly into `state.needles`' formula,
uncapped - so swapping it for a ring-width equivalent is a same-family
substitution (which lagged scalar feeds the formula), not a new
correction needing its own cap. The closest *existing* needle-side
Mäkelä correction is actually `leaf_mass_correction` itself (checks
`state.needles` against Repola's own `N_repo` target) - a real
pipe-model-shaped comparison for needles already exists, just not tied
to height or diameter.

```{r proxy-switch-leafmass, cache=TRUE}
run_proxy_leafmass <- function(growth_proxy_height) {
  CASSIA_cpp(
    weather                    = weather_1998_2022,
    site                       = "Hyde",
    pPREL                      = c(parameters_2015$pPREL, parameters_2015$N_parameters),
    parameters                 = parameters_2015$parameters_test,
    common                     = common_p,
    ratios                     = ratios_p,
    sperling                   = parameters_2015$sperling_test,
    needle_mass_in             = 0,
    Throughfall                = parameters_2015$Throughfall,
    photosynthesis_as_input    = FALSE,
    nitrogen_balance           = 25,
    nitrogen_change            = FALSE,
    nitrogen_contrast          = FALSE,
    preles                     = TRUE,
    fAPAR_Tian                 = TRUE,
    organ_level_sugar          = FALSE,
    needle_mass_grows          = TRUE,
    height_diameter_correction = TRUE,
    leaf_mass_correction       = TRUE,
    growth_proxy_height        = growth_proxy_height
  )
}

CASSIA_leafmass_height <- run_proxy_leafmass(TRUE)
CASSIA_leafmass_diam    <- run_proxy_leafmass(FALSE)

leafmass_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_leafmass_height$Growth$leaf_mass,
             proxy = "growth_proxy_height = TRUE (current)"),
  data.frame(dates = dates_1998_2022, value = CASSIA_leafmass_diam$Growth$leaf_mass,
             proxy = "growth_proxy_height = FALSE (ring width)")
)
```

```{r proxy-switch-leafmass-plot, fig.height=5}
ggplot(leafmass_long, aes(x = dates, y = value, colour = proxy)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c(
    "growth_proxy_height = TRUE (current)"     = "#1b7837",
    "growth_proxy_height = FALSE (ring width)" = "#762a83"
  )) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "5 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "Needle leaf_mass pool, both switch settings",
       subtitle = "Hyde 1998-2022, leaf_mass_correction = TRUE throughout (so leaf_mass is a real accumulating pool, not memoryless) - tracking the standing pool instead of the daily growth flux",
       x = NULL, y = "Needle leaf_mass (kg C / tree)") +
  pub_theme
```

The standing pool shows the same artifact as Sect. 2, just more visibly
because it accumulates: the two settings start close together (both
~1.4kg C in 1998) and track each other reasonably while the correction
isn't yet biting hard, with `TRUE` actually running slightly *higher*
than `FALSE` through roughly 2008. Past that point `TRUE` collapses -
by 2022 its seasonal peaks have fallen from ~2kg C to under 0.4kg C, a
decline `FALSE` never shows (it keeps the same roughly 1-2kg C seasonal
range throughout). So this isn't "one setting is always lower" - it's
that `TRUE`'s long-run decline (Sect. 2) only properly shows up in the
standing pool once it's had enough years to compound, which a snapshot
at any single early year would miss entirely. Whichever proxy is used
changes how much standing leaf mass the tree ends up carrying by 2022 -
directly relevant to anything downstream that reads `leaf_mass`
(fAPAR/LAI, the litter mechanisms in Sect. 1-3 of the Pauliina deck,
ORCHIMIC's C/N-split litter).
